reviews.title: Affordable storage
reviews.comment: I been using computers forever, and I used all brands of storage devices and so far I never had issues with Seagate drives period that's like 25yrs. I used western digital to Maxtor or Toshiba even no name brands. So far I been using these segates for most of my storage and they just work and no fuzz, I will continue to use segate drives for my storage needs.
reviews.author: NUSA

reviews.title: Surprisingly good hard drive for a refurb.
reviews.comment:
It's big, heavy and runs a little on the warm/hot side, but otherwise, this is a pretty nice drive. It passed the comprehensive SMART surface test, so that's a relief and I haven't had any troubles with it so far. Not too noisy, which is a nice plus.
What I really like though, is how fast this drive is. I wasn't expecting much, being a 5900RPM drive, but this guy copied huge disk images lickety-split with >145MB/s sustained writes all the way through. That's faster than any hard drive I've owned so far, aside from SSD's.
If the price comes down a bit, I might be tempted to buy another one of these.
reviews.author: Ed

reviews.title: Speeds are totally fine; I don't know how Reallocation works but is it like an odometer?
reviews.comment: The hours started at zero when I first checked. The caution signal is typically when there are tens of thousands of hours- I once purchased a refurbished drive with 52,000 hours on and the same yellow Caution symbol in CrystalDiskInfo. I don't know what would cause the Caution signal to be on if it has zero hours, but if you've seen Ferris Bueller's Day Off, you know the odometer can be reset. Perhaps it was done in a way that recalibrated it and extended the life. But anyways, I've had a 52,000 hour drive work fine, so it's not a big deal if this has 30,000 hours on it. But It would be nice to know if it was reset. Hence the reason four instead of 5.

reviews.title: As good as new
reviews.comment: This the second 4TB drive I have bought from DBSKY. Both passed extended tests. The first has been in service for 16 months without any problems. The manufacturing date of 2014 is to be expected for this drive, so it is about as old as the drives in the RAID that needed a replacement. The shipment was extremely well packaged.
